notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. A parable or similitude is not a dated event and is not placed in any order: the chapter states only what the ayat present as a similitude, what it is likened to, and what the ayat themselves say. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The ayah says that the similitude of those who take protectors besides God is like that of the spider, which took a house.
The ayah says that the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if they knew.

chapters.summary_md: The ayah likens those who take protectors besides God to the spider, which took a house [c1]. It adds that the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if they knew [c2].
chapters.body_md: The ayah says that the similitude of those who take protectors besides God is like that of the spider, which took a house [c1]. It adds that the frailest of houses is the house of the spider, if they knew [c2].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah names what is likened (those who take protectors besides God) and what it is likened to (the spider and its house) [c1]. It then states the point of the picture in one clause: the frailest of houses is the house of the spider [c2].
chapters.kids_md: The ayah says that those who take protectors besides God are like the spider, which took a house [c1]. The frailest of houses is the house of the spider [c2].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the picture compares reliance on protectors besides God with a house that is frail [c1][c2]. Another reading is that the ayah closes with the words if they knew [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: who the protectors are; the ayah says only protectors besides God and names none.
- Not established: what the house is made of or how the spider built it; the ayah says house and does not describe it.
- The ayah itself uses the word for a similitude (mathal).
- The Arabic awhan al-buyut is rendered 'the frailest of houses'; a scholar may prefer another wording.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: none identified; a scholar should say whether any should be linked to this ayah.
The wording of awliya as protectors and of awhan as frailest is for a scholar to confirm.
